saints.name: St. Raymond of Penyafort
saints.title: Priest
saints.shortBlurb: A Catalan Dominican and master of canon law who gathered the scattered decretals of the Church into order…
biography: Born about 1175 near Vilafranca in Catalonia, of a noble family allied to the house of Aragon, Raymond was doctor of civil and canon law and taught at Bologna before receiving the habit of the Order of Preachers in 1222, at the age of forty-seven. For confessors he wrote the Summa de casibus poenitentiae, long a standard manual.

Summoned to Rome in 1230, he served Pope Gregory IX as chaplain and grand penitentiary and gathered the decretals of a century into one ordered book, issued in 1234 as the Decretals of Gregory IX, which remained the law of the Church until the Code of 1917. Elected Master of his Order in 1238, he resigned in 1240 and returned to Spain.

He encouraged Thomas Aquinas to write the Summa contra Gentiles and founded schools of Arabic and Hebrew for converting Jews and Moors. A legend tells that, refused a ship by King James I, he sailed from Majorca to Barcelona on his cloak. He died at Barcelona on 6 January 1275, nearly a hundred, and was canonized by Clement VIII in 1601. Hence he is the patron of canon lawyers.
saints.knownFor: Compiling the Decretals of Gregory IX.
